newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-ALKER EQUALS COURSE RECORD TO WIN SOUTH AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ALKER EQUALS COURSE RECORD TO WIN SOUTH AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: New Zealander Steve Alker equalled the Kooyonga Golf Club course record on Sunday to win the South Australian Open after Australia's Wayne Grady made a hash of the 17th.
Alker fired a seven-under-par 65 to leapfrog the early leaders, including British Open champion Tom Lehman, and win by one shot from Grady. He finished on 273, 15 under par.
British Open champion Lehman, who led by one shot overnight, carded a 72 to share third place on 13 under with Craig Parry and Brett Ogle of Australia and New Zealand's Michael Long.
Former U.S. PGA champion Grady appeared on course for victory when he led by two shots with two holes remaining.
However, he had a disastrous triple bogey seven at the 17th and then missed a birdie putt at the final hole which would have forced a play-off with Alker.
Lehman also needed a birdie at the 18th to earn a play-off but pushed his chip shot well past the hole to finish with a bogey five.
Alker, who had started the final round five shots behind, was already in the clubhouse and had not expected to finish ahead of Grady and Lehman.
"All I could do was go out and shoot a low score," Alker said. "I'd like to think that the 65 was special and I'd won it...But I felt for Wayne. To have one hole like that, it's disappointing."
Grady's disaster at the 17th began when his approach shot to the green overshot its mark by 30 yards and was buried in weeds at the base of a tree.
He barely managed to move his ball at the first attempt. After making the green with his next shot, Grady's putt then lipped the hole to hand Alker the outright lead.
"No one wishes it on anyone but it's a part of golf. At the moment it's hurting quite a bit," Grady said.
Lehman surrendered his overnight lead with a bogey at the eighth, followed by a double bogey at the par-four ninth after the American's tee shot found heavy rough on the side of the fairway.
"I'm disappointed but I feel even worse for Wayne. He had it in the bag and let it get away," Lehman said.
